data.title: Nystatin
data.summary: Topical antifungals · Polyene antifungal (from Streptomyces noursei)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antifungals_

**Class:** Polyene antifungal (from Streptomyces noursei)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds ergosterol → membrane pores → leakage (fungicidal); not absorbed from gut or skin

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Candidiasis only: oral thrush (suspension), intertrigo, napkin candidiasis, candidal paronychia, vaginal candidiasis
- Combined with steroids/antibiotics in some creams

## Dose & formulations
- Cream/ointment 100,000 U/g two to three times daily; oral suspension 100,000 U/mL, 1–4 mL four times daily (swish and swallow)

## Adverse effects
- Very safe; irritation, GI upset with large oral doses

## Contraindications
- Dermatophyte infections (ineffective)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe (not absorbed).

## Viva points
- Polyene — Candida only, not dermatophytes; not absorbed orally

_Sources: Khopkar ch.19; Wolverton 4e ch.42. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
